results.summary: This project implements an 8-byte RAM using shift registers. It stores data bits and provides 8 parallel outputs. The design is written in Wokwi and uses a clock and address inputs to control data storage. The documentation is minimal, stating only that it stores stuff, and lacks detailed testing instructions.

This is a 4-bit ALU that supports eight operations and includes a built-in 4-bit accumulator register. It performs operations such as load, negate, shift right, subtract, AND, XOR, OR, and add, with the result stored in the accumulator. The design is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested using a push-button, debouncer, DIP-switch, and LEDs, as described in the documentation. The ALU outputs the accumulator value and a carry flag, and it can be reset by setting all inputs to zero.

This project converts a 4-bit binary number to either decimal or hexadecimal and displays the result on a 7-segment display. The user selects the conversion mode via dedicated input pins (Dec or Hex) and inputs the binary number through four pins. The design is implemented in Wokwi and outputs the seven segment control signals plus a dot. The documentation explains the basic operation and testing but does not provide detailed implementation details.

This project consists of eight inverters that invert every input line. It is also used to fill empty design spaces on the chip. The design is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested by setting input switches and observing the corresponding LEDs. The documentation is very brief and does not provide additional context or applications.

This project creates a random walk animation on a 7-segment display, where the active segment moves randomly. It uses a finite state machine with 14 flip-flops and a linear feedback shift register to generate randomness. A clock divider, controlled by DIP switches, slows the walk to a visible speed, and an optional flashing dot can be enabled. The design is implemented in Wokwi and is self-initializing, requiring no reset signal.

This project divides the input clock frequency by 2 raised to the power of a 4-bit binary number entered via input pins. It outputs the divided clock on a single pin. The design is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested by entering a binary number and probing the output. The documentation is very brief and lacks detailed implementation or testing information.

This project implements a 3-bit parallel adder-subtractor that can add or subtract two 3-bit binary numbers. It uses a carry-in input to select between addition and subtraction (via two's complement). The result is displayed on a 7-segment display, with outputs mapped to segments. The design is implemented in Wokwi and includes a clock and reset, though their role is not fully explained in the documentation.

This project is an asynchronous 3-bit down counter that counts through a specific sequence: 7, 3, 5, 1, 6, 2, 4, 0. It uses three flip-flops and asynchronous inputs to trigger each flip-flop in sequence. The counter value is displayed on a 7-segment display, and a DIP switch is used to provide count signals. The design is implemented in Wokwi and includes a reset input.

This project converts Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) input to decimal digits for display on a 7-segment display. It uses a decoder circuit to drive the appropriate segments based on the BCD value. The design is implemented in Wokwi and outputs the segment control signals. The documentation describes the basic operation but does not provide detailed testing instructions or pin mappings.

This project implements a 3-bit binary multiplier that computes the product of two 3-bit numbers, producing a 6-bit result. It uses full adders to sum partial products and outputs the result to a 7-segment display. The design is implemented in Wokwi and is purely combinational. The documentation explains the multiplication algorithm but lacks detailed pin mappings and testing procedures.
